headline: OPINIÓN SOBRE EDUCACIÓN UNIVERSITARIA

headline: REFLEXIÓN ACERCA DE LA VIOLENCIA CONSTITUCIONAL
content: Sumas y restas/Sandro Ventura discute la preocupante tendencia de candidatos vinculados a incidentes violentos contra mujeres ocupando lugares altos en las encuestas. headline: Accusations against Daniel Urresti for sexual assault
content: We have seen him humiliate his wife, and his behavior has revealed several times how women are considered mere consumption items, interchangeable according to political convenience.  Daniel Urresti has been accused of raping a woman twice. When confronted about these accusations, the nationalist candidate laughed and applauded.  Carlos Acuña was denounced by his former spouse for having mistreated her during their marriage years. She claims, among other things, that he would throw her down stairs whenever she found out he had another partner. Additionally, while married, Carlos impregnated a girl who was just sixteen years old, whereas he was thirty-three. His family accuses him of rape. Although later they withdrew this accusation, something terrible happened there.  Its symptomatic that five leading presidential hopefuls are linked to cases involving violence against women. This reflects poorly on our society which still endorses machismo and abuse towards women.

headline: The societal reflection through election choices
content: All those fighting daily to secure our place in the world workforce and demanding gender stereotype abolition should first deny votes to any suspect of female maltreatment. It’s inconsistent to demand equal treatment yet minimize such ‘blemishes’ in politicians come voting time. These allegations alone warrant vote denial.  If we truly desire sensitivity toward anti-woman sentiment nationally, lets not allow governance under someone potentially capable of humiliating us. Women need to lead change, being nearly half the population, holding both responsibility and power over choosing leaders defending rights.

headline: Reflections on Perus past decades
content: Memories of the eighties bring back unhappy reflections where everything collapsed – economic stability, businesses big and small, politics, ideologies, collective self-esteem, aspirations of millions across rural and urban areas. Thousands fled abroad, others succumbed between conflicting forces during terrorism era, countless resisted catastrophe following logic akin to terminal illness survival day-by-day. That experience undeniably marked us, unresolved even now.  Non-coincidentally, certain public opinions remain taboo, incessantly claiming nothing changed, corruption persists universally despite external acclaiming optimism. We justify learned survival tactics amid hyper-inflation societies: Only dancers survive. Eighties followed by nineties dismantled more than national economy and policy but diluted primary community notions. Despite growth emergence and middle-class rise, division, distrust, polarization persist within society.

headline: Artistic journey invites revisiting dark history
content: Visitors invited to travel directly to the past sans detours encounter a bleak future face-on. One feels the past hasnt passed, complaints and pessimism linger, learning to live forward remains elusive, reacting merely to shadows continues unabated. Not ready to promote fresh politician generation, bold proposals challenging mediocracy await attention. Voting patterns repeat historical figures and offers, casting ballots driven by fear rather than hope for tomorrow.

headline: Congress moves ahead with extradition treaty before executive action
content: If Ambassador Cristina Velásquez also holds French citizenship, dismissal seems warranted, states Martin Bellúndé Moreyra, former Commission Chair of Foreign Relations. Though suggesting necessary amendments upon activation, expressed intent to establish precedent beyond current terms allowing foreign offenders tried under Peruvian law. This treaty stems since 2008, always improvable regarding effectiveness and scope. Discussions around zero-tolerance policies combating terrorism ensued amidst legislative summonings explaining government objections to ratification due to perceived constitutional breaches.

headline: LEY DE AFP ESTÁ AHORA EN MANOS DEL CONGRESO
content: Ante el vencimiento del plazo para que el presidente Ollanta Humala promulgue u observe la ley aprobada por el Congreso el 3 de diciembre y que permite a los afiliados a las AFP retirar hasta el 95.5% de sus fondos al jubilarse, el gobierno decidió observar la autógrafo, con lo que ésta quedará en manos del Congreso.  Cabe recordar que la ley en mención también facultará además a que los jubilados utilicen el 25% de sus fondos como garantía para iniciar un préstamo hipotecario, así como el retiro de hasta el 50%, en casos de declaración de una enfermedad mortal. Amplía también el Regimen Especial de Jubilación Anticipada (REJA) para empleados públicos hasta el 31 de diciembre del 2018.

headline: EE.UU.: DESOCUPACIÓN CAÍDA AL 5%
content: En el año 2015 se crearon 2.95 millones de empleos en Estados Unidos; así, el desempleo se situó en 5% al finalizar el año, según información proporcionada por el Departamento de Trabajo estadounidense. Este será el segundo mejor año para la generación de empleo en dicha nación, que nota estos alentadores índices desde 1999. Por otra parte, los salarios aumentaron 2.5%. Los sectores que más trabajo crearon fueron construcción, salud y servicios; a estos últimos se les puede atribuir la generación de 142,000 empleos en diciembre.

headline: ‘MISSION COMPLETED’: LO TENEMOS CAPTURADO’ JOAQÚN GUZMÁN LOERA HA SIDO DETENIDO
content: Mission completed: we have him. With these surprising tweets, Mexican President Enrique Peña Nieto announced Joaquín ‘El Chapo’ Guzmáns capture after his escape six months ago through a tunnel spectacle. This arrest gives political relief since under his government was the last escape of the world’s most wanted drug lord. Captured for the third time during a navy-led operation, he stated it was against impunity resulting from intense intelligence work over several months.

headline: ¿POR QUÉ NO PUEDEN PERDER?
